mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 2.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and increasing equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE increasing by more than 0.2 percentage points over 3 months) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 0.5% in one month indicate weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0% and sustained for 3 months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns due to higher interest rates reducing equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO > 105.0) signals strong economic activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 255.0 indicates accelerating inflation, prompting central bank rate hikes that reduce equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 255.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS rising > 0.5% in 1 month) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE falling > 0.1pp in 1 month) signals a strong labor market, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (HOUST above the 90th percentile of its 5-year range), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as the economy approaches a peak, leading to negative returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is above the 90th percentile of its 5-year historical range.
